# Introduction

Hierarchical Orthologous Groups (HOGs) are sets of genes that have
descended from a single common ancestral gene within a taxonomic range of
interest (Altenhoff et al. 2013). Each HOG is defined with respect to a
taxonomic level; going towards more recent levels, a HOG can split into
several sub-HOGs if the ancestral gene was duplicated. HOGs thus capture
the full history of gene duplications and losses of a gene family, and they
correspond to the genes of ancestral genomes.

This vignette shows how to explore HOGs, ancestral genomes and their
synteny with `OmaDB`. See the vignette "Get started with OmaDB" for an
introduction to the package.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("OmaDB")
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(OmaDB)
```

# Retrieving HOGs

HOGs can be retrieved by their HOG ID or by one of their member proteins.
Without a level, the most specific HOG of a protein is returned, with
`level = "root"` the HOG at its deepest level.

```{r hog}
hog <- getHOG("YEAST00001")
hog[, c("hog_id", "level", "description")]

root <- getHOG("YEAST00001", level = "root")
root[, c("hog_id", "level")]
```

The HOG ID encodes the duplications: `r root$hog_id` is the root HOG,
`r hog$hog_id` one of its sub-HOGs. The sub-HOGs of the root HOG can be
found in its `children_hogs` attribute:

```{r children}
children <- root$children_hogs[[1]]
children$hog_id
```

The root HOG at the level of the *Saccharomycetaceae* thus split into two
sub-HOGs, due to a duplication of the ancestral gene. These are the
paralogs that arose from the whole genome duplication in the ancestor of
*Saccharomyces cerevisiae*.

# Members and functional annotations

The members of a HOG at a given level are retrieved with `members = TRUE`:

```{r members}
members <- getHOG(root$hog_id, level = "Saccharomycetaceae", members = TRUE)
nrow(members)
head(members[, c("omaid", "canonicalid", "oma_hog_id")])
table(members$species.code)
```

The Gene Ontology annotations of the ancestral gene can be retrieved with
`attribute = "gene_ontology"`. The score indicates how well the annotation
is supported by the annotations of the members of the HOG.

```{r hog-go}
go <- getHOG(root$hog_id, attribute = "gene_ontology")
go[, c("GO_term", "name", "aspect", "score")]
```

To test whether the GO annotations of a sub-HOG are enriched compared to
the whole family, the annotations of the members can be analysed with the
`r Biocpkg("topGO")` package:

```{r topgo, message = FALSE}
library(topGO)
memberGO <- getProtein(members$omaid, attribute = "gene_ontology")
annotations <- formatTopGO(memberGO, format = "geneID2GO")
subhog <- members$omaid[startsWith(members$oma_hog_id, children$hog_id[1])]
GOdata <- getTopGO(annotations, foregroundGenes = subhog,
    format = "geneID2GO", ontology = "BP")
GOdata
```

HOGs with a similar phylogenetic profile, i.e. a similar pattern of gene
losses and duplications, can be found with
`attribute = "similar_profile_hogs"`:

```{r similar}
similar <- getHOG(root$hog_id, attribute = "similar_profile_hogs",
    max_results = 5)
similar[, c("hog_id", "jaccard_similarity")]
```

The complete structure of a HOG, with all speciation and duplication
events, is available in the OrthoXML format:

```{r orthoxml}
xml <- getOrthoXML(root$hog_id)
cat(substr(xml, 1, 300))
```

# Ancestral genomes

All HOGs defined at a taxonomic level correspond to the genes of the
ancestral genome at that level:

```{r ancestral}
ancestral <- getHOGs(level = "Saccharomycetaceae")
nrow(ancestral)
summary(ancestral$completeness_score)
```

The members of these HOGs can be loaded using the urls in the column
`members_url` with `resolveURL()`:

```{r resolve}
head(resolveURL(ancestral$members_url[1])$members$omaid)
```

# Synteny

The OMA Browser also infers the gene order of ancestral genomes.
`getSynteny()` retrieves the neighbourhood of a HOG at a given level as a
graph, with the HOGs as nodes and edges between neighbouring HOGs:

```{r synteny}
synteny <- getSynteny(level = "Saccharomycetaceae", id = root$hog_id,
    context = 2)
synteny$nodes
synteny$links[, c("source", "target", "weight", "orientation")]
```

The graph can be analysed with graph packages such as igraph:

```{r igraph, eval = requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)}
g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(synteny$links, directed = FALSE)
igraph::degree(g)
```

orthologous groups from orthologous gene pairs. PLoS ONE 8(1): e53786.
